# Multi-LAN Router Configuration with DHCP, DNS & Web Server — Cisco Packet Tracer

A Cisco Packet Tracer lab simulating a single router (Cisco 2911) serving **two separate LANs** on different subnets, each with its own DHCP pool, plus a statically configured DNS Server and Web Server reachable from both networks.

> All screenshots below are embedded directly in this file (base64) — nothing else to upload, just paste this file as-is.

## 📌 Objectives

- Design and simulate a multi-LAN network using a single router with two subnets
- Configure two router interfaces (`Gig0/0` and `Gig0/1`) as gateways for two different LANs
- Configure the router as a DHCP server with two separate DHCP pools (with excluded addresses, default gateway, and DNS option)
- Deploy a DNS Server and Web Server with static IPs and verify domain resolution
- Verify DHCP allocation and end-to-end connectivity across both LANs

## 🛠️ Tools Used

- Cisco Packet Tracer
- 1 × Router (Cisco 2911)
- 2 × Switch (Cisco 2960-24TT)
- 6 × PC (PC-PT), 1 × Laptop (Laptop-PT)
- 1 × DNS Server, 1 × Web Server (Server-PT)

## 🌐 Network Topology

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="700"/>

| Network | Subnet Mask | Gateway | Interface | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `192.168.10.0/25` | `255.255.255.128` | `192.168.10.1` | Gig0/1 | New LAN — PC0, PC1, PC2, remote Laptop1 |
| `172.17.0.0/27` | `255.255.255.224` | `172.17.0.1` | Gig0/0 | Original LAN — PC3, PC4, PC5, DNS Server, Web Server |

DNS Server: `172.17.0.2` &nbsp;•&nbsp; Web Server: `172.17.0.3`

## ⚙️ Configuration

### 1. Gig0/0 interface (original LAN)

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="450"/>

```
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 172.17.0.1 255.255.255.224
 duplex auto
 speed auto
```

### 2. Gig0/1 interface + DHCP pool (new LAN)

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="500"/>

```
Router#en
Router#conf t
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
Router(config)#int gig0/1
Router(config-if)#no shut

%LINK-5-CHANGED: Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to up
%LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to up

Router(config-if)#ip add 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.128
Router(config-if)#ex
Router(config)#ip dhcp excluded-add 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.10
Router(config)#ip dhcp pool Seu1
Router(dhcp-config)#network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.128
Router(dhcp-config)#dns-server 172.17.0.2
Router(dhcp-config)#default-router 192.168.10.1
Router(dhcp-config)#ex
```

### 3. DHCP pool for the original LAN (172.17.0.0/27)

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="500"/>

```
!
ip dhcp excluded-address 172.17.0.1 172.17.0.3
!
ip dhcp pool Seu1
 network 172.17.0.0 255.255.255.224
 default-router 172.17.0.1
 dns-server 172.17.0.2
!
```

### 4. Verifying DHCP exclusions (`show run`)

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="550"/>

```
Router#show run
Building configuration...

Current configuration : 926 bytes
!
version 15.1
no service timestamps log datetime msec
no service timestamps debug datetime msec
no service password-encryption
!
hostname Router
!
ip dhcp excluded-address 172.17.0.1 172.17.0.3
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.10
!
ip dhcp pool Seu1
 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.128
 default-router 192.168.10.1
 dns-server 172.17.0.2
!
```

### 5. Final interface configuration (both interfaces)

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="500"/>

```
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 172.17.0.1 255.255.255.224
 duplex auto
 speed auto
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.128
 duplex auto
 speed auto
```

## 📊 Result

Both LANs successfully receive dynamic IP addresses from their respective DHCP pools, resolve `www.sajjad.com` via the DNS server on `172.17.0.2`, and load the page hosted on the Web server at `172.17.0.3` — confirming correct routing, DHCP, and DNS configuration across the whole network.
